records.source: לֵ֣ץ הַ֭יַּיןהֹמֶ֣ה שֵׁכָ֑ר וְכָל־שֹׁ֥גֶה בּ֝֗וֹ לֹ֣א יֶחְכָּֽם׃
records.gloss: A mocker [is] the wine, noisy [is] strong drink, and anyone staggering by it will not be wise.
pieces: Wine makes people mock and strong drink makes them rowdy; \q no one who reels under them is wise.

L.1: Wine [is] a mocker, strong drink [is] a brawler, \q and whoever staggers by it will not be wise.

R.1: Wine and beer make people rude and loud. \q Anyone who gets drunk is not wise.

decisions.choice: a brawler: noisy, rowdy (homeh); strong drink: fermented drink, often beer
decisions.reason: Strong drink (shekar) was made from grain or fruit. The drink is pictured as doing what it makes the drinker do: mock and brawl.

decisions.choice: staggers: reels, goes astray (shagah)
decisions.reason: The verb is used of reeling from drink (Isaiah 28:7) and of straying (5:19–20, 23).

records.source: נַ֣הַם כַּ֭כְּפִיר אֵ֣ימַת מֶ֑לֶךְ מִ֝תְעַבְּר֗וֹ חוֹטֵ֥א נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
records.gloss: A roaring like the lion [is the] terror of a king; [one] infuriating him misses his life.
pieces: A king's fury is like a lion's roar; \q anyone who angers him puts their own life at risk.

L.2: [The] terror of a king [is] like [the] roaring of a lion; \q whoever provokes him forfeits {{gender:their|his}} life.

R.2: An angry king is as frightening as a roaring lion. \q If you make him angry, you could lose your life.

decisions.choice: misses his life: forfeits his life
decisions.reason: The verb (hata) is "miss, sin"; as in 8:36, the one who does it harms his own life.

decisions.choice: like a lion's roar: as in 19:12

records.source: כָּב֣וֹד לָ֭אִישׁ שֶׁ֣בֶת מֵרִ֑יב וְכָל־אֱ֝וִ֗יל יִתְגַּלָּֽע׃
records.gloss: Honor to a person [is] cessation from strife, but every fool breaks out.
pieces: Staying out of a fight brings honor, \q but every fool is ready to burst into one.

L.3: [It is an] honor for a person to keep away from strife, \q but every fool breaks out [in a quarrel].

R.3: It is honorable to stay out of arguments. \q Fools are always ready to start one.

decisions.choice: breaks out: bursts into a quarrel
decisions.reason: The same rare verb is used in 17:14 and 18:1 of a quarrel that breaks out.

records.source: מֵ֭חֹרֶף עָצֵ֣ל לֹא־יַחֲרֹ֑שׁ וְשָׁאַ֖ל בַּקָּצִ֣יר וָאָֽיִן׃
records.gloss: From winter a sluggard does not plow; and he asks at the harvest, and there is nothing.
pieces: The lazy will not plow in the cold season; \q at harvest they look for a crop and find nothing.

L.4: Because of [the] winter, [the] sluggard does not plow; \q {{gender:they look|he looks}} [for a crop] at harvest, and there [is] nothing.

R.4: Lazy people do not plow their fields when the weather is cold. \q So at harvest time they have nothing.

decisions.choice: from winter: in the cold, rainy season when plowing is done
decisions.reason: In Israel the ground was plowed and sown after the first rains of autumn and winter. The lazy put it off because of the cold and so have no harvest.

decisions.choice: and he asks, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "he will ask"; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "and he asks". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: asks: looks for a crop, or begs
decisions.reason: He seeks a harvest where nothing was sown, or begs from others because he has none.

records.source: מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים עֵצָ֣ה בְלֶב־אִ֑ישׁ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה יִדְלֶֽנָּה׃
records.gloss: Deep waters [is] a plan in [the] heart of a person, and a person of understanding draws it out.
pieces: A person's real intentions lie deep, like water in a well, \q but someone with understanding can bring them up.

L.5: Counsel in a person's heart [is] deep water, \q but a person of understanding draws it out.

R.5: What people really think is hidden deep inside them, like water in a deep well. \q But a wise person can find it out.

decisions.choice: deep water ... draws it out: like water from a well
decisions.reason: Purposes are hidden deep (18:4), but understanding can draw them out, whether one's own or another's.

decisions.choice: like water in a well
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the well that the picture of drawing water implies.

records.source: רָב־אָדָ֗ם יִ֭קְרָא אִ֣ישׁ חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים מִ֣י יִמְצָֽא׃
records.gloss: A multitude of people proclaim each his loyalty, but a person of faithfulness, who can find?
pieces: Plenty of people speak of their own loyalty, \q but who can find one who is really faithful?

L.6: Many people proclaim each {{gender:their|his}} own loyal love, \q but a faithful person, who can find?

R.6: Many people say they are loyal friends. \q But it is hard to find someone you can really trust.

decisions.choice: loyal love ... faithful: claim set against reality
decisions.reason: Loyal love (hesed) is claimed easily; faithfulness (emunim) is proved over time. For "who can find?" compare 31:10.

records.source: מִתְהַלֵּ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֣וֹ צַדִּ֑יק אַשְׁרֵ֖י בָנָ֣יו אַחֲרָֽיו׃
records.gloss: Walking in his integrity [is] a righteous [one]; how blessed [are] his sons after him!
pieces: The righteous live with integrity; \q how blessed are their children after them!

L.7: [The] righteous walks in {{gender:their|his}} integrity; \q how blessed [are] {{gender:their|his}} {{gender:children|sons}} after {{gender:them|him}}!

R.7: Good people live honest lives. \q Their children will be truly happy after them.

decisions.choice: blessed children: the blessing passes on
decisions.reason: A parent's integrity blesses the next generation (14:26; Psalm 37:26; 112:2).

records.source: מֶ֗לֶךְ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל־כִּסֵּא־דִ֑ין מְזָרֶ֖ה בְעֵינָ֣יו כָּל־רָֽע׃
records.gloss: A king sitting on a throne of judgment [is] winnowing with his eyes all evil.
pieces: A king seated on his judgment throne \q sifts out every evil with a look.

L.8: A king who sits on [the] throne of judgment \q winnows all evil with his eyes.

R.8: When a king sits on his throne to judge, \q he can spot every evil thing and get rid of it.

decisions.choice: winnows: sifts out like chaff from grain
decisions.reason: Winnowing tossed threshed grain into the wind to blow the chaff away. A just king's searching gaze separates out wrongdoing (verse 26).

records.source: מִֽי־יֹ֭אמַר זִכִּ֣יתִי לִבִּ֑י טָ֝הַ֗רְתִּי מֵחַטָּאתִֽי׃
records.gloss: Who will say, "I have kept my heart pure; I am clean from my sin"?
pieces: Who can say, "My heart is pure; \q I am cleansed of my sin"?

L.9: Who can say, "I have kept my heart pure; \q I am clean from my sin"?

R.9: No one can honestly say, "My heart is pure. \q I have no sin."

decisions.choice: no one is free of sin
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one" (1 Kings 8:46; Psalm 51:7; Ecclesiastes 7:20).

decisions.choice: a statement
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies.

records.source: אֶ֣בֶן וָ֭אֶבֶן אֵיפָ֣ה וְאֵיפָ֑ה תּוֹעֲבַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: A weight and a weight, a measure and a measure, an abomination of YHWH [are] also both of them.
pieces: Two sets of weights, two sizes of measure: \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} detests them both.

L.10: Weight and weight, measure and measure, \q both of them alike [are] an abomination to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} hates it when people cheat by using false weights and measures.

decisions.choice: weight and weight: two different weights
decisions.reason: A dishonest trader kept a heavy weight for buying and a light one for selling (Deuteronomy 25:13–15). The measure (ephah) was a dry measure for grain.

records.source: גַּ֣ם בְּ֭מַעֲלָלָיו יִתְנַכֶּר־נָ֑עַר אִם־זַ֖ךְ וְאִם־יָשָׁ֣ר פָּעֳלֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Even by his deeds a youth makes himself known, whether pure and whether upright [is] his conduct.
pieces: Even the young show who they are by what they do, \q whether their conduct is pure and right.

L.11: Even a youth makes {{gender:themselves|himself}} known by {{gender:their|his}} deeds, \q whether {{gender:their|his}} conduct [is] pure and whether [it is] right.

R.11: Even children show what they are like by the way they act. \q You can tell if they are good and honest.

decisions.choice: makes himself known: shows his character
decisions.reason: The verb (nakar) can mean "make oneself known" or "act as a stranger, pretend" (Genesis 42:7). Most simply, actions reveal character even in the young.

records.source: אֹ֣זֶן שֹׁ֭מַעַת וְעַ֣יִן רֹאָ֑ה יְ֝הוָ֗ה עָשָׂ֥ה גַם־שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: An ear hearing and an eye seeing, YHWH has made also both of them.
pieces: The ear that hears and the eye that sees: \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is the maker of both.

L.12: [The] ear that hears and [the] eye that sees, \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has made both of them.

R.12: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} made our ears to hear and our eyes to see.

decisions.choice: the maker of ears and eyes
decisions.reason: The one who made hearing and sight hears and sees all (Psalm 94:9), and gave them to be used for wisdom (verse 13; 15:31).

records.source: אַל־תֶּֽאֱהַ֣ב שֵׁ֭נָה פֶּן־תִּוָּרֵ֑שׁ פְּקַ֖ח עֵינֶ֣יךָ שְֽׂבַֽע־לָֽחֶם׃
records.gloss: Do not love sleep lest you become poor; open your eyes; be satisfied [with] bread.
pieces: Do not love sleep, or you will end up poor; \q keep your eyes open, and you will have food to spare.

L.13: Do not love sleep, or you will become poor; \q open your eyes, [and] have your fill of bread.

R.13: Do not sleep too much, or you will become poor. \q Stay awake and work, and you will have plenty to eat.

decisions.choice: open your eyes: stay awake and alert
decisions.reason: The second command states the result of the first: wakefulness brings food (6:9–11; 19:15).

records.source: רַ֣ע רַ֭ע יֹאמַ֣ר הַקּוֹנֶ֑ה וְאֹזֵ֥ל ל֝֗וֹ אָ֣ז יִתְהַלָּֽל׃
records.gloss: "Bad, bad," says the buyer, and going away for himself, then he boasts.
pieces: "No good, no good," says the buyer, \q then goes off and boasts about the bargain.

L.14: "Bad, bad," says the buyer, \q but when {{gender:they go|he goes}} away, then {{gender:they boast|he boasts}}.

R.14: Buyers say, "This is junk!" to get a low price. \q Then they go away and brag about the good deal they got.

decisions.choice: haggling in the market
decisions.reason: The buyer runs the goods down to lower the price, then brags about the bargain. The saying observes without comment.

decisions.choice: the bargain; to get a low price
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what the buyer is boasting about and why he complained.

records.source: יֵ֣שׁ זָ֭הָב וְרָב־פְּנִינִ֑ים וּכְלִ֥י יְ֝קָ֗ר שִׂפְתֵי־דָֽעַת׃
records.gloss: There is gold and abundance of jewels, but a vessel of preciousness [are] lips of knowledge.
pieces: There is gold, and jewels in abundance, \q but lips that speak knowledge are a rarer treasure.

L.15: There [is] gold and an abundance of jewels, \q but lips of knowledge [are a] precious ornament.

R.15: Gold and jewels are valuable. \q But words that are wise are worth even more.

decisions.choice: a precious ornament: a rare treasure
decisions.reason: The word (keli) is any crafted object, here a costly piece. Compare 3:15 and 8:11.

records.source: לְֽקַח־בִּ֭גְדוֹ כִּי־עָ֣רַב זָ֑ר וּבְעַ֖ד נָכְרִיָּ֣ה חַבְלֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: Take his garment, for he has stood surety [for] a stranger, and for a foreign [woman], hold it in pledge.
pieces: Take the coat of one who puts up security for a stranger; \q if they do it for a foreign woman, hold it as a pledge.

L.16: Take {{gender:their|his}} garment, for {{gender:they have|he has}} put up security for a stranger; \q and for a foreign woman, hold it in pledge.

R.16: If people promise to pay a stranger's debts, they are a bad risk. \q Take their coat as a guarantee before you lend them anything.

decisions.choice: take his garment: demand a pledge from a rash guarantor
decisions.reason: A lender could hold a garment as a pledge (Exodus 22:26–27). Anyone foolish enough to guarantee a stranger's debt (6:1–5) is a poor risk, so secure the loan. The saying returns in 27:13.

decisions.choice: a foreign woman, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "foreigners"; the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "a foreign woman", as in 27:13. The point is the same.

decisions.choice: they are a bad risk
decisions.reason: Readable states the reason for taking a pledge, which the saying implies.

records.source: עָרֵ֣ב לָ֭אִישׁ לֶ֣חֶם שָׁ֑קֶר וְ֝אַחַ֗ר יִמָּֽלֵא־פִ֥יהוּ חָצָֽץ׃
records.gloss: Sweet to a person [is] bread of falsehood, but afterward his mouth will be filled [with] gravel.
pieces: Bread won by deceit tastes sweet at first, \q but afterward it fills the mouth with grit.

L.17: Bread gained by falsehood [is] sweet to a person, \q but afterward {{gender:their|his}} mouth will be filled with gravel.

R.17: Things you get by cheating may seem good at first. \q But later they will be like a mouthful of sand.

decisions.choice: bread of falsehood: gain gotten by deceit
decisions.reason: Compare the stolen water and bread of 9:17. The pleasure turns to grit (Lamentations 3:16).

records.source: מַ֭חֲשָׁבוֹת בְּעֵצָ֣ה תִכּ֑וֹן וּ֝בְתַחְבֻּל֗וֹת עֲשֵׂ֣ה מִלְחָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: Plans by counsel are established, and by guidance make war.
pieces: Make your plans firm by taking counsel, \q and wage war only with wise guidance.

L.18: Plans are established by counsel, \q and by wise guidance wage war.

R.18: Get good advice before you make plans. \q Do not start a war without wise guidance.

decisions.choice: guidance: skillful steering, strategy (tahbulot)

records.source: גּֽוֹלֶה־סּ֭וֹד הוֹלֵ֣ךְ רָכִ֑יל וּלְפֹתֶ֥ה שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִתְעָרָֽב׃
records.gloss: Uncovering secret counsel [is one] going about [as] a slanderer, and with [one] opening his lips do not mix.
pieces: A gossip goes around giving away secrets, \q so have nothing to do with a person who cannot keep their mouth shut.

L.19: One who goes about slandering reveals secrets; \q so do not associate with one who opens {{gender:their|his}} lips [wide].

R.19: Gossips tell other people's secrets. \q So stay away from people who talk too much.

decisions.choice: opens his lips: talks too freely
decisions.reason: The verb (patah) means "open wide" and is related to "simple". It points to a babbler who cannot keep a confidence. Compare 11:13.

records.source: מְ֭קַלֵּל אָבִ֣יו וְאִמּ֑וֹ יִֽדְעַ֥ךְ נֵ֝ר֗וֹ בֶּאֱשׁ֥וּן חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
records.gloss: [One] cursing his father and his mother, his lamp will go out in [the] time of darkness.
pieces: Those who curse their father or mother \q will have their lamp snuffed out in deep darkness.

L.20: Whoever curses {{gender:their|his}} father or {{gender:their|his}} mother, \q {{gender:their|his}} lamp will go out in [the] time of darkness.

R.20: If you curse your father or your mother, \q your life will end in darkness.

decisions.choice: in the time of darkness, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: in the pupil of darkness (the written form)
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "in the pupil of darkness", that is, the very middle of the dark (as in 7:9); the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "in the time of darkness". Both mean the deepest dark.

decisions.choice: his lamp will go out: his life and line will end
decisions.reason: See 13:9 and 24:20. The law made cursing parents a capital crime (Exodus 21:17).

records.source: נַ֭חֲלָה מְבֹהֶ֣לֶת בָּרִאשֹׁנָ֑ה וְ֝אַחֲרִיתָ֗הּ לֹ֣א תְבֹרָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: An inheritance hastily gained at the first, and its end will not be blessed.
pieces: An inheritance grabbed too early \q will not be blessed in the end.

L.21: An inheritance gained in haste at [the] beginning, \q its end will not be blessed.

R.21: If you grab an inheritance too soon, \q it will not bring you good in the end.

decisions.choice: gained in haste, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) give a rare verb meaning to loathe or be greedy (Zechariah 11:8); the reading the scribes marked (qere) is "hastily gained". Both describe grasping at an inheritance.

decisions.choice: seizing an inheritance before its time
decisions.reason: Perhaps a son who forces his father to hand over his share early (19:26; Luke 15:12).

records.source: אַל־תֹּאמַ֥ר אֲשַׁלְּמָה־רָ֑ע קַוֵּ֥ה לַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה וְיֹ֣שַֽׁע לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Do not say, "I will repay evil"; wait for YHWH, and he will save you.
pieces: Do not say, "I will pay back this wrong!" \q Wait for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rescue you.

L.22: Do not say, "I will repay evil"; \q wait for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will save you.

R.22: Do not say, "I will get even!" \q Wait for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to help you. He will save you.

decisions.choice: leave vengeance to the LORD
decisions.reason: See 24:29; Deuteronomy 32:35; Romans 12:17–19.

records.source: תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה אֶ֣בֶן וָאָ֑בֶן וּמֹאזְנֵ֖י מִרְמָ֣ה לֹא־טֽוֹב׃
records.gloss: An abomination of YHWH [are] a weight and a weight, and balances of deceit [are] not good.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} detests two sets of weights; \q cheating scales are wrong.

L.23: Weight and weight [are] an abomination to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and deceitful scales [are] not good.

R.23: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} hates it when people use false weights. \q Cheating with scales is wrong.

decisions.choice: repeats verse 10
decisions.reason: See verse 10 and 11:1.

records.source: מֵיהוָ֥המִצְעֲדֵי־גָ֑בֶר וְ֝אָדָ֗ם מַה־יָּבִ֥ין דַּרְכּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: From YHWH [are the] steps of a man, and a person, what will he understand [of] his way?
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} directs each person's steps, \q so how can anyone make sense of where they are going?

L.24: [The] steps of {{gender:a person|a man}} [are] from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q how then can anyone understand {{gender:their|his}} own way?

R.24: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} guides every step people take. \q So how can they fully understand their own lives?

decisions.choice: God guides steps humans cannot fully understand

records.source: מוֹקֵ֣שׁ אָ֭דָם יָ֣לַע קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְאַחַ֖ר נְדָרִ֣ים לְבַקֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: A snare of a person [is to] say rashly "Holy!" and after vows to reflect.
pieces: It is a trap to declare something holy without thinking \q and to have second thoughts only after making the vow.

L.25: [It is] a snare for a person to say rashly, "Holy!" \q and [only] after [making] vows to reflect.

R.25: Do not make promises to God without thinking. \q It is a trap to promise something and then try to change your mind later.

decisions.choice: "Holy!": dedicating something to God
decisions.reason: Saying "Holy!" set an offering apart for God (Leviticus 27). A rash vow binds the one who makes it (Ecclesiastes 5:4–6).

decisions.choice: promises to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the vow and the dedication as a promise made to God.

records.source: מְזָרֶ֣ה רְ֭שָׁעִים מֶ֣לֶךְ חָכָ֑ם וַיָּ֖שֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם אוֹפָֽן׃
records.gloss: Winnowing wicked [ones is] a wise king, and he brings back over them a wheel.
pieces: A wise king sifts the wicked like grain \q and rolls the threshing wheel over them.

L.26: A wise king winnows [the] wicked \q and rolls [the threshing] wheel over them.

R.26: A wise king finds out who is evil \q and punishes them hard, like a farmer threshing grain.

decisions.choice: winnowing and the threshing wheel
decisions.reason: Grain was crushed by a wheeled cart or sledge and then winnowed (Isaiah 28:27–28). The king first sifts out the wicked (verse 8), then crushes them.

records.source: נֵ֣ר יְ֭הוָה נִשְׁמַ֣ת אָדָ֑ם חֹ֝פֵ֗שׂ כָּל־חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן׃
records.gloss: [The] lamp of YHWH [is the] breath of a human, searching all [the] chambers of [the] belly.
pieces: The human spirit is the lamp of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q shining into every hidden part of a person.

L.27: [The] lamp of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is the] breath of a human, \q searching all [the] chambers of [the] belly.

R.27: The spirit {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave each person is like {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} lamp. \q It shines into the hidden places of the heart.

decisions.choice: the breath of a human: the life-breath God gives, the human spirit
decisions.reason: The word (neshamah) is the breath God breathed into the first man (Genesis 2:7). Here it is the inner self, aware of itself, like what is called conscience (compare 1 Corinthians 2:11).

decisions.choice: the human spirit is the LORD's lamp, searching the inner person
alternatives: the LORD's lamp searches the human spirit
decisions.reason: Most simply, the spirit God gave is the lamp by which a person's inmost self is searched out, by God and before God. The line can also be read as God's lamp searching the human spirit.

decisions.choice: the chambers of the belly: the innermost self
decisions.reason: As in 18:8 and 26:22.

records.source: חֶ֣סֶד וֶ֭אֱמֶת יִצְּרוּ־מֶ֑לֶךְ וְסָעַ֖ד בַּחֶ֣סֶד כִּסְאֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Loyalty and faithfulness preserve a king, and he upholds by loyalty his throne.
pieces: Loyal love and faithfulness keep a king safe; \q by loyal love he makes his throne secure.

L.28: Loyal love and faithfulness guard [the] king, \q and by loyal love he upholds his throne.

R.28: A king who is loyal and faithful will be safe. \q His kingdom will last because he is kind and loyal.

decisions.choice: loyal love and faithfulness: as in 3:3
decisions.reason: Hesed and emet may be the king's own virtues or God's loyal love guarding him; both are true of a good reign (16:12; 29:14; Isaiah 16:5).

records.source: תִּפְאֶ֣רֶת בַּחוּרִ֣ים כֹּחָ֑ם וַהֲדַ֖ר זְקֵנִ֣ים שֵׂיבָֽה׃
records.gloss: The glory of young men [is] their strength, and the splendor of old [ones is] gray hair.
pieces: Young men take pride in their strength; \q the old wear gray hair as their honor.

L.29: [The] glory of young men [is] their strength, \q and [the] splendor of [the] old [is] gray hair.

R.29: Young people are proud of being strong. \q Old people can be proud of their gray hair.

decisions.choice: strength and gray hair: each age has its honor
decisions.reason: Gray hair stands for long life and the wisdom it brings (16:31).

records.source: חַבֻּר֣וֹת פֶּ֭צַע תַּמְר֣וּק בְּרָ֑ע וּ֝מַכּ֗וֹת חַדְרֵי־בָֽטֶן׃
records.gloss: Wounds of bruising [are] a cleansing in evil, and blows [to the] chambers of [the] belly.
pieces: Blows that wound scour away evil, \q and beatings cleanse the inner self.

L.30: Bruising wounds [are] a scouring away of evil, \q and blows [scour the] chambers of [the] belly.

R.30: Painful punishment can wash away evil. \q It can make a person good on the inside.

decisions.choice: a cleansing, as the scribes' reading has it
decisions.reason: The ketiv and qere spell this noun differently; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: painful correction scours away evil
alternatives: wounds are a cosmetic for the evil person
decisions.reason: The line is terse. The noun (tamruq) is used of beauty treatments (Esther 2:3), here of scrubbing clean. The point seems to be that hard discipline reaches the inner self.
